Leading the pack is **Hamilton**, which continues to earn near-universal acclaim nearly a decade after its debut. Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop retelling of American history remains as revolutionary and relevant as ever, proving its staying power as a modern theatrical masterpiece. Close behind is **Maybe Happy Ending**, a charming robot love story that critics celebrate as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, bringing genuine emotional depth to an unlikely premise.

The variety on display this March is striking. **Oh, Mary!** delivers absurdist comedy with Cole Escola's riotous reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy cabaret dreamer, while **Ragtime** offers timely social commentary through its acclaimed revival. Long-running favorites like **The Lion King**, **Chicago**, and **The Book of Mormon** continue to demonstrate why they've become Broadway institutions, each maintaining critical approval through distinctive artistic visions.

Musical theater fans can also find everything from the folk-opera storytelling of **Hadestown** to the technical wizardry of **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child**, plus the infectious rhythms of **Buena Vista Social Club**. Whether you're drawn to innovative new voices or time-tested spectacles, this month's Broadway landscape provides compelling options across genres and styles. Browse the full rankings below to find the perfect show for your theatrical tastes.

The show's influence on the theatrical landscape remains unmatched nearly a decade after its debut.

Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a critical darling with an 85/100 score, captivating reviewers with its unexpectedly poignant story of two robots discovering love and humanity. The top ten also features enduring spectacles like **The Lion King**, which continues to mesmerize audiences with Julie Taymor's iconic puppetry and design work, and the timely **Ragtime** revival, which earns praise for Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance and the score's emotional resonance with contemporary audiences. Close behind, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** continues to captivate audiences with its theatrical magic and technical prowess, though reviewers remain divided on the strength of its narrative.

Whether you're drawn to sharp comedy, magical stagecraft, or intimate drama, March 2026 offers compelling options across Broadway's diverse theatrical spectrum. Consider your preferences for scale, tone, and subject matter when selecting your next theater experience.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theatrical ambition cut short by unprecedented circumstances. While the pandemic curtailed many of these productions' original runs, their artistic achievements continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike.

Leading our selections is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, where this grittier reboot earns an 83/100 critical score. The production demonstrates how classic musicals can be successfully reinvented for contemporary audiences, though purists remain divided on the approach.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as perhaps the most significant rediscovery of the year, finally bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway after decades. With 29 reviews averaging 78/100, this stellar revival proves the work's examination of race, power, and identity remains urgently relevant. Meanwhile, **Grand Horizons** offers lighter fare—a boulevard comedy featuring powerhouse performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell that critics find pleasant if somewhat predictable.

The more experimental entries prove divisive: Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcases luminous acting in a chamber piece that doesn't convince all critics of its theatrical necessity, while Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining generates the widest critical split, with some praising its bold vision and others finding it at odds with the material's essence.

With an average critical score of 75/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 demonstrates both artistic ambition and the enduring challenge of balancing innovation with tradition. Whether you're drawn to bold reinterpretations or classical revivals, these productions offer distinct perspectives on Broadway's evolving identity.

# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theatrical ambition cut short by unprecedented challenges. Despite the season's abrupt interruption, these five productions left lasting impressions on critics and audiences alike.

Leading the pack is **Les Misérables**, which scores 83/100 across 9 reviews for its grittier reimagining at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This rebooted production takes a darker approach to the beloved musical's themes, earning praise from most critics, though the radical departure doesn't resonate with everyone.

**A Soldier's Play** follows closely with 78/100 from 29 reviews, marking a powerful and long-overdue Broadway debut for Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama. Critics consistently highlight the stellar revival's examination of race, power, and justice within the military, finding the work as relevant today as when it was written.

The remaining productions offer varied experiences: **Grand Horizons** (73/100) delivers familiar but well-crafted comedy elevated by Jane Alexander's performance; **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100) divides critics despite Laura Linney's universally praised solo turn; and **West Side Story** (68/100) polarizes audiences with Ivo van Hove's radical reimagining of the classic.

With an average score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 Broadway season demonstrates both the enduring power of established works reimagined and the continued relevance of important American dramas. Whether you're drawn to bold reinterpretations or powerful storytelling, this guide will help you discover which of these productions best matches your theatrical interests.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2021 stands as a watershed moment in theater history—marking not just the industry's triumphant return from pandemic shutdown, but also a creative renaissance that pushed theatrical boundaries in remarkable ways.

The year's productions earned an impressive average critic score of 81/100, with several shows redefining what's possible on Broadway stages. Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance recreating his mother's harrowing kidnapping ordeal. Critics hail it as one of the most innovative theatrical experiments in recent memory.

**The Lehman Trilogy** stands as another towering achievement, with Sam Mendes' epic drama tracing 163 years of American capitalism through one family's rise and fall. The production's extraordinary performances and stunning stagecraft cement its status as a theatrical landmark. Meanwhile, **Pass Over**, Antoinette Chinonye Nwosu's powerful drama blending Beckett and Exodus, made history as Broadway's first show to reopen post-pandemic, earning praise for its urgent examination of Black male experience in America.

The season also saw bold reimaginings of classics, including a gender-swapped **Company** that revitalized Sondheim's masterwork and Rebecca Frecknall's immersive **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**, which completely transformed the August Wilson Theatre into a nightclub experience. Experimental works like **Is This a Room**, constructed entirely from FBI transcripts, proved that verbatim theater could be as gripping as any thriller.

Whether you're discovering these groundbreaking productions for the first time or revisiting theatrical history, these ten shows represent Broadway at its most daring and essential.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2022 stands out as a watershed moment for American theater—a year when the industry roared back from pandemic shutdowns with remarkable artistic vitality. The ten productions featured in this guide, averaging an impressive 83/100 critical score, represent some of the most acclaimed work to grace Broadway stages in recent memory.

The year proved particularly notable for its celebration of new musicals alongside essential revivals. **Kimberly Akimbo** leads our rankings with near-universal critical acclaim, praised for its delicate balance of comedy and heartbreak in telling the story of a teenager with a rare aging condition. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offered audiences a stripped-down reimagining of Sondheim's classic that critics hailed as both a fitting tribute to the late composer and a vital reinterpretation in its own right. Meanwhile, **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, broke new ground with its brazenly honest exploration of a Black gay artist's inner life.

Perhaps most striking about 2022's lineup is the prominence of Pulitzer Prize winners—five productions on this list earned theater's most prestigious honor, either recently or in years past. From Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** to Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, the season offered audiences an embarrassment of riches when it came to essential dramatic works.

Whether you're catching these productions during their current runs or exploring what made 2022 such a landmark year for Broadway, this guide provides comprehensive critical context for the season's most important shows.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the 2023 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period for theatrical storytelling, with an impressive average critic score of 82/100 across our top ten plays. The year delivered everything from long-awaited revivals to bold new works that continue to resonate with audiences today.

Leading the pack is Maria Friedman's acclaimed revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which finally gives Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop the production it deserves. Critics praise its emotionally resonant staging, proving that some shows simply need the right moment and vision to succeed. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** demonstrates that theatrical adaptations of popular IP can transcend mere fan service when executed with technical brilliance and genuine dramatic weight.

The season also showcases powerful contemporary voices. **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama featuring Sarah Paulson, earns recognition as a modern masterpiece, while **Purlie Victorious** proves that Ossie Davis's 1961 satire remains bracingly relevant more than six decades later. Meanwhile, **Parade**'s revival arrives with urgent timeliness, and **Fat Ham** brings its Pulitzer-winning reimagining of Hamlet to Broadway with raucous energy.

From Alex Edelman's solo tour de force **Just for Us** to Jodie Comer's commanding Broadway debut in **Prima Facie**, the year demonstrates the enduring power of intimate storytelling alongside grand-scale productions like Josh Groban's **Sweeney Todd** and the music-filled **Buena Vista Social Club**.

Whether you're revisiting these productions during their extended runs or discovering recordings and future revivals, these ten plays represent essential theatrical experiences from a standout Broadway year.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 84/100 critic score—represents some of the most innovative and emotionally resonant theater to reach New York stages in recent years.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's immersive rock drama set in a 1970s recording studio, which critics consistently describe as a theatrical marvel for its authentic portrayal of the creative process. The production's meticulous attention to period detail and its exploration of artistic collaboration have made it a benchmark for contemporary playwriting.

Musical theater also sees significant reinvention in this lineup. **Maybe Happy Ending** brings an unexpectedly touching robot love story to Broadway, earning praise as one of the most original musicals in years. Meanwhile, **CATS: The Jellicle Ball** demonstrates how radical reimagining can breathe new life into established properties, infusing the Andrew Lloyd Webber classic with ballroom culture and high-energy choreography that critics find liberating.

Comedy finds its champion in **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln that transforms the former First Lady into a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist. The farce has become a word-of-mouth sensation for its fearless irreverence.

From intimate character studies like **Mary Jane** to lavish revivals such as **Oliver!** and **Gypsy**, this collection showcases Broadway's range and artistic ambition. Whether you're drawn to experimental dance-theater hybrids or crowd-pleasing ensemble pieces, these critically acclaimed productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater this season.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves into March 2026, the season showcases an impressive range of productions that opened throughout 2025, from bold reimaginings of American classics to innovative new works pushing theatrical boundaries. This month's top ten plays—averaging a strong 84/100 from critics—demonstrate the breadth and vitality of contemporary theater.

Leading the pack is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread acclaim for transforming Arthur Miller's classic into a visceral, emotionally devastating experience through minimalist staging and exceptional ensemble work. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** reminds audiences why this quirky musical became a beloved fixture, with critics praising its airtight construction and surprising emotional depth.

Family-friendly fare also makes a strong showing with **Paddington The Musical**, which enchants critics through its remarkably lifelike puppet work, while Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning **English** brings intellectual rigor and sensitivity to questions of language and identity. Meanwhile, **Ragtime** returns with renewed urgency, powered by Joshua Henry's commanding performance and Terrence McNally's timeless score.

The season reflects Broadway's continued commitment to diverse storytelling, from Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's incisive family drama **Purpose** to Itamar Moses's feminist memory play **Liberation**. Even unconventional entries like the darkly comic **Dead Outlaw**—chronicling the bizarre posthumous journey of outlaw Elmer McCurdy—find critical support for their theatrical audacity.

Whether you're drawn to classic revivals reimagined for contemporary audiences or bold new voices challenging theatrical conventions, this season offers compelling reasons to return to Broadway.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings an intimate start to the year's new Broadway plays, with a focus on solo performance that proves less can indeed be more.

Leading the pack is **Every Brilliant Thing**, where Daniel Radcliffe delivers what critics describe as a disarmingly warm performance in this interactive one-person show. The production tackles the weighty subject of depression through an unexpectedly life-affirming lens, cataloging small joys and moments of beauty that make existence worthwhile. With an impressive 81/100 critic score across 19 reviews, Radcliffe's ability to connect with audiences—often breaking the fourth wall and inviting participation—demonstrates his range beyond the blockbuster franchises that made him famous. Critics consistently highlight his genuine charm and the show's delicate balance between humor and heartbreak.

While 2026's Broadway play offerings have started modestly in terms of quantity, the quality bar remains high. This year appears to be favoring intimate theatrical experiences over large-cast productions, with **Every Brilliant Thing** exemplifying how a single performer and a powerful script can create an evening as impactful as any sprawling ensemble piece.

The season is still young, and with several months remaining, theatergoers can expect additional productions to open as spring progresses into summer. For now, those seeking meaningful, emotionally resonant theater will find Radcliffe's performance offers exactly the kind of human connection that makes live theater irreplaceable. Check back regularly as more 2026 productions open and critics weigh in on the year's theatrical landscape.
